Cut a zuint vector into intervals

Source: R/reduce.R
zu_cut.Rd

cut() of a zuint or decimal128() vector compares each value with the breaks exactly, so values beyond 2^53 fall in the interval they belong to. Base cut() reads such a vector's raw bits.

Arguments

x

A zuint or decimal128 vector.

breaks

At least two breaks, in any order.

labels

NULL for the default labels, FALSE for integer codes, or one label for each interval.

include.lowest

Whether the lowest break (the highest, when right = FALSE) belongs to its interval.

right

Whether the intervals are closed on the right.

dig.lab

Accepted for compatibility; the labels are not rounded.

ordered_result

Whether the factor is ordered.

...

Not used.

Value

A factor, or an integer vector for labels = FALSE; NA for a value outside every interval and for NA.

Details

The arguments are those of base::cut.default(). breaks is a zuint vector or a number vector, in any order; the values are compared with it as x > b and x <= b are, never through a double. The default labels write each break in full, so dig.lab is accepted and not used.

A single number of intervals as breaks is refused with a zuint_unsupported_error: base derives the breaks from the range with a fractional step, which a vector of integers cannot hold. Give the breaks. Breaks that are NA, repeated or not numbers, a labels vector of the wrong length and a flag that is not TRUE or FALSE are a zuint_type_error.

Examples

x <- int64(c("9007199254740993", "9007199254740994", "-5"))
cut(x, int64(c("-10", "9007199254740993", "9007199254740995")))
#> [1] (-10,9007199254740993]              (9007199254740993,9007199254740995]
#> [3] (-10,9007199254740993]             
#> Levels: (-10,9007199254740993] (9007199254740993,9007199254740995]
cut(x, c(-10, 0, 1e16), labels = FALSE)
#> [1] 2 2 1
